header.title: VOLLEYBALL RULES
header.subtitle: Simplified FIVB regulation — the essential rules to understand and play.

warning: This page is an educational summary. For official competitions, refer to the official FIVB regulation.
quickFaults: Double contact by the same player
Back-row attack above the net from the front zone
Foot fault on the serve (stepping on the line)

rules.title: Match format
rules.content: A match is played as best of 5 sets. Each set is played to 25 points with at least a 2-point lead. If a 5th set is needed, it is played to 15 points.

rules.title: Teams
rules.content: 6 players per side on court. A team can have up to 6 substitutes and one libero. Maximum 6 regular substitutions per set (libero not counted).

rules.title: Serve
rules.content: The serve is performed from the service zone behind the back line. The ball must cross the net into the opponent's court. The server has 8 seconds after the whistle to strike. A serve that touches the net and falls into the opponent's court is GOOD (let serve legal since 2001).

rules.title: Point on every rally
rules.content: Since 1999 (rally point system), a point is scored on every rally, regardless of which team served. The scoring team gets the serve.

rules.title: Maximum 3 touches
rules.content: A team has up to 3 touches to return the ball. The block does not count as a team touch — the team still has 3 touches after a block.

rules.title: Double contact
rules.content: A player cannot contact the ball twice in a row, except on the first team contact (reception/dig). Exception for the block. New 2025-2026 FIVB trial: double contact allowed on the set (2nd touch) as long as the ball stays on the same side.

rules.title: Net fault
rules.content: Touching the net during the action of playing the ball is a fault. Touching outside the action or outside the antennae is not a fault. Partially crossing under the net is allowed if it does not interfere with the opponent. FIVB 2025 goal: "promote flowing play".

rules.title: Ball on the lines
rules.content: A ball that lands on the line is "in". A ball that crosses outside the antennae or outside the crossing space is out.

rules.title: Mandatory rotation
rules.content: On every side-out, the team winning the serve rotates clockwise: P2→P1, P3→P2, P4→P3, P5→P4, P6→P5, P1→P6. The player going P2→P1 becomes the new server.

rules.title: Position fault
rules.content: At the moment the server strikes, players must respect their rotation order (no diagonal overlap). Fault = point + serve to the opponent. 2025 update: the overlap rule now only applies to the RECEIVING team — the serving team can position freely.

rules.title: 3-meter rule
rules.content: Back-row players (P1, P5, P6) cannot attack above the net from the front zone. They can jump from behind the 3 m line and land in the front zone — this is legal.

rules.title: Libero
rules.content: The libero wears a contrasting jersey and only plays back-row (P1, P5, P6). Unlimited uncounted substitutions. Cannot block or attack above the net. May serve since 2021 in a single rotation per set. May be captain since 2021. Restriction: if the libero hand-sets from the front zone, a teammate cannot attack the ball above the net.

rules.title: Time-outs
rules.content: Each team has 2 time-outs of 30 seconds per set. Automatic technical time-outs at the 8th and 16th points in sets 1-4 are used in some FIVB competitions.

rules.title: Serve — key rules
rules.content: 8 seconds to strike after the whistle. Only one toss allowed, but the server can let the ball drop once without penalty. Foot fault: at the moment of contact (or jump take-off), the server must not touch the back line or court. Screen on serve: teammates must not raise their hands above their heads during the serve (2025 rule).

rules.title: Back-row attack
rules.content: A back-row player can attack if their take-off is behind the 3 m line (both feet). They can also strike the ball if any part is below the net. Blocking or attacking the serve above the net from the front zone is a fault.

rules.title: Held ball
rules.content: Contact with the ball must be brief and clean. "Ugly contact ≠ fault": imperfect contact is not automatically a fault if the ball rebounds. More permissive standard for forearm passes than for hand sets.

rules.title: Overlap: only on reception
rules.content: Since 2025, the overlap rule only applies to the receiving team. The serving team can occupy any position on the court at the moment of the serve.

rules.title: No screen on serve
rules.content: Players on the serving team are now forbidden from raising their hands above their heads during the serve until the ball crosses the net. Such a screen is sanctioned directly.

rules.title: Double contact on the set — trial
rules.content: FIVB 2025-2026 trial: double contact on the set (2nd touch) is allowed as long as the ball remains on the same side. If the trial succeeds, the rule could become permanent.

rules.title: Libero can serve (since 2021)
rules.content: The libero can serve since 2021 in a single rotation per set. Rule varies by federation (some USAV and NFHS tournaments do not allow it — check the competition regulation).
